subject: ophthalmology
title: Ocular injuries

steps.tx: **Chemical burns** grade by limbal ischaemia and corneal clarity (Roper Hall, Dua): **alkalis** (lime, ammonia) saponify penetrating deeply needing prolonged irrigation, while **acids** coagulate precipitating a barrier limiting depth. First aid is immediate copious irrigation (water or saline litres, evert lids sweeping particles) with pH testing to neutrality before history; emergency adds debridement, ascorbate and citrate debates, brief steroids with tetracyclines, amniotic membrane and stem cell transplantation for limbal failure. Symblepharon and dry eye scar late.
steps.say: Burnt eye: irrigate litres first, ask later. Alkali melts deeper than acid.

steps.tx: **Open globe** rules: shield without pressure, nil by mouth, tetanus, antiemetics, no drops or protruding tissue manipulation, CT for foreign bodies, urgent primary repair (wounds closed layer by layer, lens and vitreous addressed secondarily). **Berlin oedema** (commotio retinae whitening) observes; choroidal rupture (crescent streaks concentric to disc) watches for new vessels; traumatic optic neuropathy (RAPD after blunt trauma with initially normal disc) gets megadose steroid debates with canal decompression selected. Endophthalmitis prophylaxis starts at repair.
steps.say: Cut eye open: shield it, starve it, tetanus it, scan it, sew it. Never press or pull.

steps.tx: **Hyphaema** layers blood in the anterior chamber after blunt trauma (torn iris root, ciliary vessels); grading by height guides admission, with sickle cell trait or disease rebleeding catastrophically even at low pressure. Management is head elevation, shield, cycloplegics, cautious steroids and pressure control (avoid carbonic anhydrase inhibitors in sickle disease); rebleed peaks around day five with total black ball hyphaema threatening corneal staining. Corneal blood staining (yellow green discoloration) needs prompt washout with pressure control.
steps.say: Layered blood after a knock: shield upright, watch sickle closely. Black ball blood stains cornea fast.

steps.tx: **Retained intraocular foreign bodies** (hammering metal, farm debris, gunshot pellets) localise by CT (metal) or ultrasound and MRI debates for nonmetallic; iron siderosis (heterochromia, mydriasis, cataract, pigmentary retinopathy with extinguished ERG) and copper chalcosis (sunflower cataract, Kayser Fleischer ring) demand prompt vitrectomy removal. Sympathetic ophthalmia threatens the fellow eye after repair (see uveitis wave). **Blowout fractures** trap muscle (oculocardiac bradycardia in children needing urgent release); retrobulbar haemorrhage with tense proptosis needs lateral canthotomy before vision dies.
steps.say: Metal on metal eye injury: scan for fragments, remove iron before it rusts the retina. Tight proptosed eye after trauma: cut the canthus.
